issues.description: All chains were composed exclusively of males or exclusively of females, yet the manuscript provides no justification for this design choice and does not analyze or report whether there were differences between male and female chains. This is particularly problematic given the discussion claim that 'These findings generalize beyond the single-sex chain compositions used here, suggesting cultural transmission operates similarly in mixed-gender collaborative settings' — a claim made without any empirical basis, as mixed-gender chains were never tested.
issues.quote: In each treatment, participants were part of 14 chains each containing 5 individuals (exclusively males or exclusively females).

issues.description: The discussion makes an explicit generalizability claim about mixed-gender settings that is entirely unsupported by the data. The study only used sex-segregated chains and never tested mixed-gender chains, making this claim unwarranted.
issues.quote: These findings generalize beyond the single-sex chain compositions used here, suggesting cultural transmission operates similarly in mixed-gender collaborative settings.

issues.description: The authors acknowledge that no statistical methods were used to pre-determine sample sizes and justify their sample size only by comparison to previous publications. Without a power analysis, it is unclear whether the study was adequately powered to detect meaningful differences between treatments, particularly for the comparison of understanding scores across treatments (Analysis 4) and the interaction effects.
issues.quote: No statistical methods were used to pre-determine sample sizes but our sample sizes (i.e. number of independent chains) are larger than those reported in previous publications

issues.description: The results report wheel speed increases in 'm/h' (meters per hour) as the unit for the generation effect (mean = 5.37 m/h), but later report absolute speeds of ~123.6 m/h and ~145.7 m/h. For a 1-meter track, these speeds in m/h seem implausibly low if interpreted literally (a speed of 145.7 m/h means the wheel takes about 24.7 seconds to travel 1 meter). The units appear inconsistent or potentially erroneous — the actual speeds may be in different units (e.g., cm/s) or the reported unit is wrong.
issues.quote: The average wheel speed produced by first generation participants on their last trial was 123.6 m/h (95% Highest Posterior Density Interval: (117.3, 130.6))... After 5 generations, average wheel speed increased to 145.7 m/h

issues.description: The claim of '71% optimization after only four cultural generations' is not clearly derived from the reported numbers. If maximum speed is ~154 m/h, generation 1 speed is 123.6 m/h, and generation 5 speed is 145.7 m/h, the improvement is (145.7-123.6)/(154-123.6) = 22.1/30.4 = 72.7%. However, the text says 'about 154 m/h' for maximum speed while the payoff formula uses MaxSpeed = 160. The discrepancy between these values (154 vs 160) is unexplained and affects the optimization calculation.
issues.quote: Given that the maximum possible speed was about 154 m/h, these results indicate an optimization of 71% after only four cultural generations.

issues.description: The payoff formula uses MaxSpeed = 160, but the results section states the maximum possible speed was 'about 154 m/h'. These values are inconsistent. If the true maximum is 154, then the payoff formula uses an incorrect value; if the true maximum is 160, then the optimization calculation is wrong.
issues.quote: Given that the maximum possible speed was about 154 m/h... with MaxSpeed = 160, MinSpeed = 96

issues.description: The authors deviated from their preregistered analysis 4 because the preregistered model did not converge. While they disclose this deviation, the replacement analysis (aggregating inertia and centre-of-mass scores) fundamentally changes what is being tested and could mask treatment effects on specific dimensions of understanding. The non-convergence itself may indicate model misspecification issues that warrant further investigation.
issues.quote: However, analyses revealed that understanding scores about inertia and centre of mass were negatively correlated... As a result, the preregistered model did not converge so we ran our analysis on aggregated score and removed the terms associated the variable 'Physical Principle' in the reported model.

issues.subcategory: aggregated understanding score masks dimensional differences
issues.description: By aggregating understanding scores across inertia and centre-of-mass dimensions (due to the preregistered model not converging), the analysis obscures the very pattern the authors later highlight in exploratory analyses — that inherited theories shift understanding toward one dimension at the expense of the other. The aggregated score makes it appear that understanding doesn't change, when in fact the composition of understanding changes substantially.
issues.quote: participants' understanding again barely changed across generations, although participants in the very last generation had a slightly better understanding when they had inherited a theory

issues.description: The authors explicitly state that data collection and analysis were not performed blind to conditions. The experimenter physically set up the wheel configurations and was present during trials, creating potential for experimenter demand effects or differential treatment of participants across conditions.
issues.quote: Data collection and was not performed blind to the conditions of the experiments.

issues.description: The analyses of how inherited theories affect exploration patterns and dimension-specific understanding (Figure 3) are described as 'exploratory analyses' but constitute a major portion of the results and are central to the paper's narrative. These post-hoc analyses involve categorizing participants into subgroups based on inherited theory type, creating small and unequal subgroups (N=15, 17, 6, 18) that may lack statistical power and are susceptible to multiple comparison issues.
issues.quote: Exploratory analyses, however, reveal striking differences between treatments in participants' exploration behavior

issues.subcategory: very small subgroup sizes in exploratory analyses
issues.description: The exploratory analyses break participants into subgroups based on inherited theory type, resulting in very small samples: N=15 (inertia theory), N=17 (centre-of-mass theory), N=6 (full theory), N=18 (irrelevant theories). The full theory group (N=6) is particularly small, making any inferences from this subgroup unreliable.
issues.quote: 15 inherited an inertia-related theory, 17 inherited a centre-of-mass-related theory, 6 inherited a full theory and 18 inherited diverse, irrelevant theories.

issues.subcategory: missing statistical tests for exploratory claims
issues.description: The exploratory analyses about the effects of inherited theories on exploration patterns and understanding (Figure 3) are described qualitatively without formal statistical tests. Claims about participants who inherited different theory types showing different exploration patterns and understanding scores are supported only by visual inspection of heat maps and bar charts, not by statistical comparisons.
issues.quote: Participants who inherited an inertia theory mainly produced compact and balanced wheels... In contrast, participants who inherited a centre-of-mass theory produced unbalanced wheels with their top and right weights at extreme positions

issues.subcategory: understanding measure limited to two dimensions
issues.description: The understanding test only measures knowledge of two physical principles (moment of inertia and centre of mass). Participants may have developed other forms of causal understanding (e.g., about friction, spoke orientation, weight distribution patterns) that are not captured by this binary measure. The test also uses a forced-choice format that may not capture the richness or accuracy of participants' causal models.
issues.quote: The test comprised 10 pairs of wheels: 5 in which wheels varied in their moment of inertia, 5 in which wheels varied in the position of their centre of mass.

issues.description: With 10 questions and 3 possible answers each ('Wheel 1', 'Wheel 2', 'No difference'), the expected score for random guessing would be approximately 3.33 (10/3). The reported scores hover around 4.5, which is only modestly above chance. This raises questions about whether the understanding measure is sensitive enough to detect meaningful causal understanding, and whether the claim that participants lack causal understanding is partly an artifact of measurement insensitivity.
issues.quote: their understanding score was 4.60 (95% HPDI: (3.83, 5.53))... Horizontal line shows expected score for random guessers.

issues.subcategory: confound between theory content and chain performance
issues.description: In the Configurations + Theory treatment, the content of inherited theories is not independent of the configurations that are also transmitted. Participants who discovered good configurations related to inertia would likely write inertia-related theories and transmit inertia-optimized configurations. The effects attributed to theory transmission may partly reflect the configurations that co-traveled with those theories.
issues.quote: In the 'Configurations + Theory' treatment (n =70), participants additionally received the previous participant's theory about the physical system.

issues.description: The sample consists entirely of French university students, which the authors partially acknowledge. However, the abstract and main conclusions make broad claims about human cultural evolution and technology optimization without adequately qualifying these claims. The authors note this limitation only briefly in the discussion.
issues.quote: we asked successive 'cultural generations' of participants (French university students) to optimize a physical system

issues.description: Chains of only 5 generations provide a limited window into cumulative cultural evolution. While significant improvement was observed, the claim that 'complex technologies need not result from enhanced causal reasoning' is based on a very short evolutionary timescale. It remains possible that causal understanding becomes important over longer chains or for more complex technologies.
issues.quote: Participants were organized into chains of 5 individuals.

issues.description: For Analysis 1, the authors state that the final model was selected after comparing several candidate models, but do not report what candidate models were compared, what criteria were used for selection, or the results of the model comparison.
issues.quote: The final model specification was selected after comparing several candidate models based on fit to the observed data.

issues.subcategory: model output details in supplementary only
issues.description: All model outputs are relegated to supplementary tables, and the main text only reports selected credible intervals. Key information such as posterior distributions, effective sample sizes, convergence diagnostics (Rhat values), and model fit statistics are not reported in the main text.
issues.quote: see Supplementary Table 1 for model output

issues.description: The results section inconsistently reports '95% Confidence Intervals' and '95% Highest Posterior Density Intervals' for what appear to be outputs from the same Bayesian models. These are different interval types, and the inconsistent terminology suggests either a reporting error or confusion about the statistical framework being used.
issues.quote: Generation 95% Confidence Intervals: (1.58, 9.02)... The average wheel speed produced by first generation participants on their last trial was 123.6 m/h (95% Highest Posterior Density Interval: (117.3, 130.6))

issues.subcategory: fixed test order may introduce order effects
issues.description: All participants received the same 10 understanding test pairs in the same order. This could introduce order effects, fatigue effects, or learning effects that systematically bias understanding scores. Randomizing the order across participants would have been more appropriate.
issues.quote: All participants were exposed to the same 10 pairs of wheels in the same order.

issues.subcategory: theory written before test phase completed
issues.description: In the Configurations + Theory treatment, participants wrote their theory before completing the understanding test. This means the act of formulating a theory could have influenced their test performance, creating a confound between treatment conditions. Participants in the Configurations treatment did not engage in this theory-articulation exercise before the test.
issues.quote: Participants were asked to write their theory before the test phase was completed.

issues.description: The manuscript mentions wheels that 'did not descend' (failures) and shows failure counts in Figure 2A. For Analysis 1, data were restricted to last two trials 'to limit the occurrence of wheels that did not descend,' while Analysis 3 assigned failed wheels a speed of 0. The different handling of failures across analyses is not well justified and could affect results differently.
issues.quote: Wheels that did not go down were attributed a speed of 0. Data were restricted to participants' last two trials in order to limit the occurrence of wheels that did not descend in the dataset.

issues.subcategory: cannot distinguish lack of understanding from measurement insensitivity
issues.description: The central claim that optimization occurs 'without causal understanding' rests on the understanding measure showing no improvement. However, participants may have developed implicit or partial causal understanding that the 10-question forced-choice test fails to capture. The absence of evidence for understanding improvement is not strong evidence for the absence of understanding improvement.
issues.quote: we show that a physical artifact becomes progressively optimized across generations of social learners in the absence of explicit causal understanding

issues.subcategory: low-dimensional task limits generalizability to complex technologies
issues.description: The authors acknowledge the task is 'low-dimensional' and frame this as a 'conservative test.' However, this framing is debatable. A 2-dimensional optimization problem may be solvable through simple trial-and-error, while genuinely complex technologies (bows, kayaks) involve many interacting dimensions where causal understanding might be essential. The conservative test argument assumes that if understanding isn't needed for simple problems, it won't be needed for complex ones — but the opposite could be true.
issues.quote: the optimization problem is low-dimensional, which provides a conservative test of our hypotheses, compared to the many-dimensional problem of optimizing, for example, the performance of a bow

issues.description: While Cohen's kappa values are reported for theory coding (0.81 and 0.85), the manuscript does not describe how disagreements between the three raters were resolved to arrive at final theory classifications.
issues.quote: Cohen's kappa coefficients reveal almost perfect agreement between raters (0.81 for inertia and 0.85 for centre of mass).

issues.subcategory: Cohen's kappa for three raters unclear
issues.description: Cohen's kappa is designed for two raters, but three raters coded the theories. The manuscript reports single kappa values without specifying whether these are averages across pairs, or whether a multi-rater statistic (e.g., Fleiss' kappa) was used.
issues.quote: 3 individuals blind to the research question were explained the dynamics of the wheel... Cohen's kappa coefficients reveal almost perfect agreement between raters (0.81 for inertia and 0.85 for centre of mass).

issues.description: Participants were told they were part of a chain and that their performance affected the next participant's outcomes. This knowledge, combined with the instruction that their last two trials would be transmitted, may have caused participants to behave more conservatively in later trials (sticking with good configurations rather than exploring), which could affect both optimization trajectories and understanding development.
issues.quote: Participants were told that they were part of a chain and so that the task was a collective one... they were informed that their last two configurations will be transmitted to the next participant in the chain

issues.subcategory: theory character limit may constrain theory quality
issues.description: Theories were limited to 340 characters, which may have artificially constrained participants' ability to express multidimensional theories. The finding that participants mainly produced 'simplistic models related to a salient dimension' could partly be an artifact of this character limit rather than reflecting genuine cognitive limitations.
issues.quote: Theories had to be less than 340 characters long and always started with 'The wheel covers the distance faster when...'.

issues.description: Analysis 3 references Supplementary Table 3 and Analysis 4 references Supplementary Table 6, skipping Tables 4 and 5. While these may exist in the supplementary materials, the gap in numbering without explanation is potentially confusing and may indicate missing or misnumbered references.
issues.quote: see Supplementary Table 3 for model output... see Supplementary Table 6 for model output

issues.description: There is a grammatical error/typo in the methods section where 'Data collection and was not performed blind' appears to be missing a word.
issues.quote: Data collection and was not performed blind to the conditions of the experiments.

issues.description: Only the last two configurations (and scores) from each participant were transmitted to the next generation. This severely limits the information available to learners and may underestimate the role of causal understanding in real cultural transmission, where much richer information (including failed attempts, verbal instruction, demonstration) is typically available.
issues.quote: All participants (except those in the first generation) were provided with the last two configurations and associated scores of the previous participant in their chain so as to simulate overlapping generations.

issues.subcategory: credible interval for interaction barely excludes zero
issues.description: The Generation x Treatment interaction for understanding scores has a 95% CI of (0.03, 0.81), which barely excludes zero. The authors interpret this as showing that 'participants in the very last generation had a slightly better understanding when they had inherited a theory' but then conclude 'these analyses do not provide substantial support for the idea that the transmission of explicit causal theories affects... individual understanding.' This interpretation is inconsistent — the interval technically excludes zero, suggesting an effect.
issues.quote: Generation x Treatment 95% CI: (0.03, 0.81), mean = 0.44... Thus, these analyses do not provide substantial support for the idea that the transmission of explicit causal theories affects wheel optimization and individual understanding.
